gap.statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (side : Fin n → Bool) (I : Fin k → Finset (Fin n)), (∀ a b : Fin n, G.Adj a b → side a ≠ side b) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ¬ (G.Adj a b ∧ G.Adj b c ∧ G.Adj c d ∧ G.Adj d a)) → 2 ≤ k → (∀ j : Fin k, ∀ a ∈ I j, ∀ b ∈ I j, ¬ G.Adj a b) → (∀ v : Fin n, ∃ j : Fin k, v ∈ I j) → (∀ v : Fin n, ∃ j : Fin k, v ∉ I j) → (∀ j : Fin k, (I j).card + 2 ≤ n) → (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → ¬ G.Adj a b → ∃ j : Fin k, a ∈ I j ∧ b ∈ I j) → ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), (∀ a b : Fin n, G.Adj a b → a ∈ T ∨ b ∈ T) ∧ G.edgeFinset.card + T.card + 1 ≤ ∑ j : Fin k, (n - (I j).card)
gap.context: SKETCH: No proof is in hand; this is a pure counting question. Let c(v) be the number of the sets that leave v out: the right side is the sum of c(v), every c(v) is at least 1, and on every edge c(u) + c(v) is at least k since no set holds both ends. For a non-adjacent pair the sets leaving out u and those leaving out v do not exhaust all k. Try induction deleting one vertex with its edges, and find where the absence of a 4-cycle is needed. Size: open, hours; a counterexample goes to the negation on this desk. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
